title_en: Some rulings on the tarāwīḥ prayer
body_ar:
هل الأفضل القيام بالتراويح في الجماعة أم في المنزل؟ وهل نستطيع أن نزيد على ثلاث عشرة ركعة؟ وإذا كان الجواب لا فبم التعبد إذن؟

أن الأفضل صلاة التراويح في المسجد، لأن حديث أبي ذر فيه من قام مع الإمام حتى ينصرف كتب له قيام ليلة، ومع ذلك إذا كان الإنسان سيزيد عما يصليه الناس في المسجد فينبغي أن يصلي في بيته لأن أفضل صلاته في بيته إلا المكتوبة، ولهذا فإن رسول الله(ص) أقر الناس على الصلاة معه في الليالي الثلاث التي قامها بالناس، ثم كان يصلي معه بعض الأفراد في غير ذلك، فقد قام معه ابن مسعود قياما طويلا جدا حتى قال ابن مسعود حتى هممت بأمر سوء، قالوا وما هو يا بن أم عبد قال هممت أن أجلس، وكذلك قام معه يعلى بن أمية، وقام معه ابن عباس ليلة مبيته عند ميمونة، وقام معه حذيفة بن اليمان عدة ليال، فهؤلاء كانوا يقومون الليل مع رسول الله(ص)..

فلذلك الأجر الوارد في الجماعة الراجح من الأحاديث إن شاء الله تعالى أنه موعود به في الفريضة وفي النافلة، وبالأخص في قيام رمضان الذي كان من سنة الخلفاء إظهاره شعيرة من شعائر الإسلام يجتمع الناس إليه في المسجد كما فعل ذلك عمر وعثمان وعلي ومن تبعهم من الخلفاء في مختلف العصور، وقد قال رسول الله(ص): «فعليكم بسنتي وسنة الخلفاء الراشدين المهديين» وبالنسبة للعدد ليس للتراويح عدد محدد ولا لقيام الليل عدد محدد، بل قال تعالى: والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما، فمن استطاع أن يقوم الليل كله فلا حرج عليه في ذلك، وقد كان بعض أصحاب رسول الله(ص) يصلون مائة ركعة، وبعضهم يصلي مائتي ركعة، وكان حزب علي بن الحسين بن علي رضي الله عنهم مائتي ركعة كل ليلة، يصلي مائتي ركعة غير الوتر كل ليلة، وبالنسبة لصلاة النبي(ص) الراجح فيها عدم التحديد أيضا بشيء، فقد قام ليلة كاملة بآية واحدة كما في حديث عائشة، وأما حديث عائشة الذي فيه حصر ذالك بقولها: ما زاد رسول الله(ص) في رمضان ولا في غيره على إحدى عشرة ركعة، وفي رواية على اثنتي عشرة ركعة بعدها الوتر، فهذا الحديث فيه تعارض في العدد حيث قالت إحدى عشرة ركعة، وفي رواية أخرى اثنتي عشرة ركعة بعدها الوتر، وأيضا فهي تحدث عما علمت وعدم العلم بالشيء ليس علما بعدمه ولم يكن النبي(ص) يبيت عندها في كل ليلة، وأيضا فقد روى عنه أصحابه أكثر من ذلك، ففي حديث أبي ذر أنه قام بهم ثلث الليل وفي ليلة أخرى ثلثي الليل، وفي ليلة أخرى حتى خشينا أن يفوتنا الفلاح، فهذا يقتضي كثرة صلاته(ص) وبالأخص أنه كان في حديث عائشة في العشر الأواخر يحيي ليله كله، فلذلك ليس للتراويح عدد محدد بالنص، ولا لقيام الليل عدد محدد بالنص، بل قال قتادة بن دعامة السدوسي: أقل ذلك حلب شاة، أي القدر الذي يحتلب فيه الإنسان شاة هذا أقل قيام الليل، ولا حد لأكثره، وكذلك فإن تحديد عمر رضي الله عنه ثلاثا وعشرين ركعة للناس ليس سنة مستمرة، بل غيرها عمر بن عبد العزيز فجعلها تسعا وثلاثين ركعة، ثم أعادها مالك بن أنس إلى ثلاث وعشرين في أيامه، فلذلك لا حرج في الزيادة والنقص، لكن المهم أن يقوم الإنسان ما يسمى قياما، أما الذي ينقر وينقش ويرجع إلى بيته كأن شيئا لم يحصل ولم يتأثر قلبه ولم يسمع قرآنا ولم يبك ولم يتعظ فهذا لم يقم الليل، والذي قام ولو لم يقم به إلا الوتر لكنه اتعظ وأطال وأوتر بتسع أو بسبع أو بخمس أو بثلاث كما كان رسول الله(ص) يفعل فهذا إن شاء الله تعالى يرجى أن يكون قد قام الليل وهذا المطلوب.
body_en:
Is it better to perform the tarāwīḥ in congregation or at home? And can we add to thirteen rakʿahs? If the answer is no, then by what act of worship [should one draw near to God]?

It is better to pray the tarāwīḥ in the mosque, because in the hadith of Abu Dharr: whoever stands with the imam until he departs, the standing of a whole night is written for him. Even so, if a person is going to add to what the people pray in the mosque, he ought to pray in his house, because the best of a person's prayer is in his house, except for the obligatory prayer. For this reason the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, approved the people's praying with him on the three nights on which he led them in standing, and thereafter certain individuals would pray with him. Ibn Masʿud stood with him for a very long standing, until Ibn Masʿud said: "until I resolved upon an evil thing." They said: "And what was it, O son of Umm ʿAbd?" He said: "I resolved to sit down." Likewise Yaʿla ibn Umayyah stood with him; Ibn ʿAbbas stood with him on the night he spent at Maymunah's; and Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman stood with him several nights. These used to stand the night with the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace..

So the reward that is reported for the congregation — the stronger view from the hadiths, God Most High willing, is that it is promised both in the obligatory prayer and in the voluntary, and especially in the standing of Ramadan, the making manifest of which, as one of the emblems of Islam, with people gathering to it in the mosque, was part of the sunnah of the caliphs, as ʿUmar, ʿUthman and ʿAli did, and those of the caliphs who followed them in the various eras. The Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, said: "Hold fast to my sunnah and the sunnah of the rightly guided caliphs." As for the number, there is no fixed number for the tarāwīḥ and no fixed number for the standing of the night. Rather God Most High has said: {and those who spend the night before their Lord prostrating and standing} (Sūrat al-Furqān 25:64). So whoever is able to stand the whole night, there is no blame upon him in that. Some of the Companions of the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, used to pray a hundred rakʿahs, and some of them would pray two hundred rakʿahs; and the daily portion (ḥizb) of ʿAli ibn al-Husayn ibn ʿAli, may God be pleased with them, was two hundred rakʿahs every night — he would pray two hundred rakʿahs besides the witr every night. As for the prayer of the Prophet, upon whom be peace, the stronger view concerning it is likewise that it was not fixed at any number: he stood a whole night with a single verse, as in the hadith of ʿA'ishah. As for the hadith of ʿA'ishah in which she confines it, saying: "The Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, never added, in Ramadan or outside it, upon eleven rakʿahs" — and in another narration, "upon twelve rakʿahs, after which was the witr" — this hadith contains a conflict in the number, since she said eleven rakʿahs, and in another narration twelve rakʿahs after which was the witr. Moreover, she reports what she knew, and not knowing a thing is not knowledge of its non-existence; and the Prophet, upon whom be peace, did not spend every night with her. Moreover, his Companions have narrated more than that from him: in the hadith of Abu Dharr, that he stood with them a third of the night, and on another night two-thirds of the night, and on another night until we feared that we would miss al-falāḥ. This entails that his prayer, upon whom be peace, was extensive — especially as, in the hadith of ʿA'ishah, he would in the last ten nights keep his whole night in vigil. For this reason there is no number fixed by an explicit text (naṣṣ) for the tarāwīḥ, and no number fixed by an explicit text for the standing of the night. Rather Qatadah ibn Diʿamah al-Sadusi said: "The least of that is the milking of a ewe" — that is, the amount of time in which a person milks a ewe; this is the least of the standing of the night, and there is no limit to the most of it. Likewise ʿUmar's fixing of twenty-three rakʿahs for the people, may God be pleased with him, is not a continuing sunnah; rather ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz changed it and made it thirty-nine rakʿahs, and then Malik ibn Anas returned it to twenty-three in his own days. For this reason there is no blame in adding or in diminishing. But what matters is that a person perform a standing that deserves the name of standing. As for the one who pecks and scratches [at his prayer] and returns to his house as though nothing had happened — his heart unmoved, having heard no Qur'an, not having wept, not having taken admonition — this one has not stood the night. And the one who stood, even if he performed nothing of it but the witr, yet took admonition and prolonged it, and prayed the witr with nine or with seven or with five or with three, as the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, used to do — this one, God Most High willing, may be hoped to have stood the night, and this is what is sought.

flags.context: وفي ليلة أخرى حتى خشينا أن يفوتنا الفلاح — in the hadith of Abu Dharr
options: until we feared that we would miss al-falāḥ [the pre-dawn meal]
until we feared that we would miss the pre-dawn meal (suḥūr)
until we feared that we would miss success
flags.note: The commentators gloss al-falāḥ in this report as the suḥūr, the pre-dawn meal, on the ground that the muezzin's call ḥayya ʿalā al-falāḥ comes near that time; the narration is in Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i. But the Sheikh does not gloss it here, and the literal sense ('success') is also grammatically available. Option 0 keeps the Arabic and offers the standard gloss in brackets without asserting it as the Sheikh's own; option 1 asserts the gloss and option 2 would make the sentence hard to follow. The Sheikh's office should say which he intends.

flags.context: أما الذي ينقر وينقش ويرجع إلى بيته كأن شيئا لم يحصل
options: the one who pecks and scratches [at his prayer]
the one who rushes through it in pecks and scrapes
the one who performs it hurriedly and perfunctorily
flags.note: Naqara ('to peck', as a bird pecks) is the classical idiom for rushing the prostrations, from the hadith forbidding 'the pecking of a crow'. Yanqush ('scratches, scrapes') is paired with it here as an intensifier and is not a standard idiom; it may be dialectal. Option 0 keeps the image, which the Sheikh clearly intends; option 2 explains it away and loses the force.

flags.arabic: وإذا كان الجواب لا فبم التعبد إذن؟
flags.context: the third limb of the question, on what one should do if adding to thirteen rakʿahs is not permitted
options: If the answer is no, then by what act of worship [should one draw near to God]?
If the answer is no, then what is the act of worship in that case?
If the answer is no, then in what does the worship consist?
flags.note: The Arabic 'fa-bima al-taʿabbud idhan' is elliptical. The premise it rests on does not arise, since the Sheikh answers that there is no fixed number, so the limb is left unanswered in the source and no answer has been supplied.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

The double dot at the end of the first paragraph is in the source. It marks the CMS 'intro text' break; the text continues below it in this record and is not truncated. No download link is offered for this item and the text ends with a completed sentence, so it is not an excerpt.
'The stronger view' renders al-rājiḥ, the view the Sheikh considers preponderant on the evidence. Where he says al-rājiḥ he is stating his own preference and the English keeps that visible.

The Sheikh disputes the restrictive hadith of ʿA'ishah on three grounds: a conflict between its narrations, the limits of her knowledge, and contrary narrations from other Companions. The reasoning chain is preserved in full rather than compressed into its conclusion.
'Emblems of Islam' renders shaʿāʾir, the visible public marks of the religion.
The verse reference at al-Furqān 25:64 has been supplied per house style; the source gives the verse text alone and without brace brackets.
